root_cause.text: ceph_mdsc_build_path() in the Ceph MDS client failed to release the temporary path buffer allocated with __getname() on several error-return paths where ownership was never transferred via path_info.path, causing memory leaks.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds missing __putname(path) calls before returning from error cases after negative ret/len checks and before returning -ENAMETOOLONG, while the commit message explicitly states that error code paths “did not free the ‘path’ pointer obtained by __getname()” unless ownership was passed to the caller.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the allocated path buffer on the ret < 0 error path in ceph_mdsc_build_path to prevent a memory leak.
intent_record.what: A call to __putname(path) was added in the error-handling branch where ret < 0, after dput(parent) and dput(cur) and before returning ERR_PTR(ret).
intent_record.how: This releases the previously allocated path buffer when the function exits due to that error condition, preventing the buffer from being leaked during runtime on this failure path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the allocated path buffer on ceph_mdsc_build_path() failure to avoid leaking memory in the len < 0 error path.
intent_record.what: In the error path inside ceph_mdsc_build_path(), after dput(parent) and dput(cur) when len < 0, the change adds a call to __putname(path) before returning ERR_PTR(len).
intent_record.how: This releases the previously allocated path buffer when path construction fails, preventing a memory leak on that negative-length error path while preserving the existing error return behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the allocated path buffer before returning ENAMETOOLONG in ceph_mdsc_build_path() to fix an error-path memory leak.
intent_record.what: A call to __putname(path) was added immediately before returning ERR_PTR(-ENAMETOOLONG) in the overlong-path error branch of ceph_mdsc_build_path().
intent_record.how: This releases the previously allocated path buffer when the function detects that the constructed path would exceed Linux path length limits, preventing a memory leak on that error path.

grouping_result.intent: Free the allocated path buffer before returning ENAMETOOLONG in ceph_mdsc_build_path() to fix an error-path memory leak.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix error-path memory leaks in ceph_mdsc_build_path() by freeing the allocated path buffer before returning on failure conditions.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly fix the identified root cause by freeing the temporary buffer allocated with __getname() on ceph_mdsc_build_path() error-return paths where ownership was not transferred, preventing the documented memory leaks.

candidates.rationale: This error return exits ceph_mdsc_build_path() on the ret < 0 path without freeing the temporary buffer allocated by __getname(), directly causing the leak described in the root cause.
This error return exits on the len < 0 failure path before ownership of the temporary path buffer is transferred, so the __getname()-allocated buffer is leaked.
This ENAMETOOLONG error path returns without releasing the temporary path buffer, matching the root cause of leaked __getname() memory on failure.

vuln_statements.explanation: This error return is taken after the temporary path buffer allocated with __getname() exists, but before ownership is transferred via path_info.path. Returning here without freeing that buffer causes the leak described in the root cause.

On the len < 0 failure path, this statement exits ceph_mdsc_build_path() while the __getname()-allocated temporary buffer is still owned locally and has not been released or transferred, resulting in a memory leak.
This ENAMETOOLONG error return leaves the temporary path buffer allocated by __getname() unreleased on an error path where ownership was never transferred to path_info.path, causing the memory leak.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the body of ceph_mdsc_build_path() and its error returns clearly enough to evaluate the leak. The function allocates a temporary buffer with `path = __getname();` near the start, but in the newly added encrypted-name branch there are multiple direct error returns before ownership is transferred or `path` is freed. Specifically: after `parent = dget_parent(cur);`, `ret = __fscrypt_prepare_readdir(d_inode(parent)); if (ret < 0) { dput(parent); dput(cur); return ERR_PTR(ret); }` and later `len = ceph_encode_encrypted_fname(...); if (len < 0) { dput(parent); dput(cur); return ERR_PTR(len); }`. In both cases, the function returns without releasing the buffer obtained from `__getname()`. The root-cause condition described in the vulnerability is therefore present: temporary path buffer allocated by `__getname()` is not released on several error-return paths where ownership was never transferred. There is no corresponding fix here such as `__putname(path)` / freeing `path` on those error paths, so the function still contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 550f7ca98ee028a606aa75705a7e77b1bd11720f
Author: Max Kellermann <max.kellermann@ionos.com>
Date:   Mon Nov 18 23:28:28 2024 +0100

    ceph: give up on paths longer than PATH_MAX
    
    If the full path to be built by ceph_mdsc_build_path() happens to be
    longer than PATH_MAX, then this function will enter an endless (retry)
    loop, effectively blocking the whole task.  Most of the machine
    becomes unusable, making this a very simple and effective DoS
    vulnerability.
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the relevant error-return paths inside ceph_mdsc_build_path() where temporary resources are handled. The root cause is failure to release the temporary path buffer allocated with __getname() on error paths before ownership is transferred. In this function body, there are direct error returns at lines 2758-2763 and 2765-2771: `ret = ceph_fscrypt_prepare_readdir(d_inode(parent)); if (ret < 0) { dput(parent); dput(cur); return ERR_PTR(ret); }` and `len = ceph_encode_encrypted_fname(...); if (len < 0) { dput(parent); dput(cur); return ERR_PTR(len); }`. These returns exit the function immediately after only dropping dentries; there is no cleanup of the temporary `path` buffer before returning. Since ownership has not been transferred here (the function is still building into local `path`), these are exactly the vulnerable leak paths described. The shown code does not contain any fix such as freeing/releasing `path` (e.g. via __putname(path)) before these error returns, so the fix is not present.
